To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a good run placement policy is workload dependent; (2) the best run placement policy for a given workload is the policy that uses a subset of the disks for writing the output run while the rest of disks are used for parallel prefetching of input runs; and (3) if buffer thrashing is avoided, the best performance is achieved with a run placement policy in which the output run does not share any disks with its own input runs

(1) with buffer thrashing, the performance of the run placement policies is workload dependent, (2) without buffer thrashing, a run placement policy with a proper number of write disk can achieve the best performance and (3) with buffer thrushing avoidance, the run placement policy that allows the output run of one merge to share the same disks with the input runs of some other merges is the best one.

(1) a good performance of concurrent mergesorts with parallel prefetching is possible with a proper subset of write disks and (2) the proper number of the write disks is workload and buffer thrashing dependent.

the design and evaluation of the run placement policy for concurrent mergesorts using the parallel prefetching technique.
the problem of how to optimally place the initial runs (input) and the final runs (output) of a merge on disks in a concurrent mergesort using parallel prefetching.
the design and analysis of the performance of concurrent mergesort algorithms for parallel disks.

a proper placement of the input runs is essential to achieve a good system performance, and the placement of the output runs should be done carefully to avoid buffer thrashing.
the performance of the merge phase of a parallel mergesort can be significantly improved by a proper choice of run placement policy and buffer thrashing avoidance.
the performance of concurrent mergesorts is very sensitive to the run placement policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the run placement policy is crucial to the performance of concurrent mergesorts on disks and that the proper choice of the run placement policy can be used to avoid buffer thrashing.

, in order to avoid buffer thrashing, the run placement policy for concurrent mergesorts using prefetching should be carefully designed to take into consideration the number of disks dedicated for writing and reading the runs, the number of input runs, and the workload.
, with proper run placement, the merge phase of a concurrent mergesort can achieve a good level of parallelism even with a large number of disks and with a relatively small number of input runs.
